Sam — great to hear and thanks for the clear asks. I put together two concise options (attached) and a short note on batching/cache/quantization impact: RDW-Optimize-Price-Table-v3.xlsx and quantization-impact-analysis.pdf. High level: 

- Credits model: upfront prepaid credits with tiered unit price. Best if you want budget predictability and to avoid monthly invoices. Credits convert at close to list unit economics; unused credits roll for 6 months.
- Committed discount model: commit monthly average throughput for 12 months, get a 12–18% baseline discount depending on tier, plus additional SLO credits for uptime. Better for sustained load.

Batching and caching notes (short):
- Prefix/KV caching reduces generation token count ~12–28% depending on prompt reuse; higher for chat with long contexts.
- Adaptive batching reduces per-token compute by coalescing similar-length requests; helps at peak (>500 concurrent req/s) with limited latency impact when using our latency-aware batcher.
- Both combined yield ~20–35% unit-cost savings in typical enterprise chat workloads. See attached analysis for modeled numbers.

Quantization guidance: we recommend the following profile for production (balance of perf vs quality):
- 4-bit quant (Q4_0) for embedder and smaller chat models where throughput matters — expect ~1–2% eval delta for embeddings, <1% for generation BLEU-like metrics in our tests.
- 8-bit fallback for long-context or safety-sensitive routes.

On the 20% concession question — we can consider a hybrid: 15% off list for a 6mo pilot in exchange for a firm 12-month renewal at a committed tier (with a step-down schedule tied to committed volume). Alternatively, apply a $XK runway-credit (applied to consumption) and keep standard committed-discount tiers. I'll loop in Ben for commercial specifics.

Next step: Ben will share a clean counterproposal (pricing table + MAP) and Laura can sign off on any exceptions. If it helps, I'll include a short mutual-action-plan doc for procurement.

Thanks — Vanessa
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
